summary: fi_resolve_issues_file never looks for an existing ledger. It always targets docs/found-issues.md in git mode and $PWD/.found-issues.md in local mode, so log/defer/resolve/promote-deferred create a second ledger that shadows the real one.
failure_scenario: A git repo keeps its ledger at <root>/.found-issues.md. pre-branch-delete.sh:186-188 and fi_find_issues_file (parse-entries.sh:32) both support this layout. Running `found-issues log src/a.py:1 — x` creates docs/found-issues.md with a fresh header and appends there. fi_find_issues_file checks docs/ first (parse-entries.sh:28), so every old entry disappears from status, list, sync and the SessionStart injection. `defer`/`resolve`/`promote-deferred` read the new empty file, answer 'no [open] entries match', and still create the stray file. Local mode has the same flaw: `log` run from a subdirectory writes $PWD/.found-issues.md there instead of the parent ledger that walk-up finds.
evidence: bin/found-issues:224-230: `if [[ "$mode" == "local" ]]; then target="$PWD/.found-issues.md" else repo_root=...; target="$repo_root/docs/found-issues.md"`; :232-242 creates the file when missing. Compare parse-entries.sh:28-35, which finds docs/found-issues.md first and then .found-issues.md while walking up.
suggested_fix: In fi_resolve_issues_file, call fi_find_issues_file first and use its result when it finds one. Only create a new ledger when nothing is found. Also stop mutating commands (defer/resolve/promote-deferred) from creating a ledger on the no-match path.
needs_runtime_repro:
mktemp -d; git init; printf '# x

- [open] 2026-10-01 a.py:1 — old
' > .found-issues.md; run `found-issues log b.py:2 — new`; then `ls docs/` and `found-issues list`. Expect docs/found-issues.md to exist and list to show only 'new'.

summary: cmd_log builds its dedup key from its own reading of the location. fi_parse_entry reads the written entry differently when the location has whitespace or a Repo:path:line shape. The keys never match, so every re-log appends a duplicate.
failure_scenario: `log 'docs/my notes.md:12 — stale'` twice. The writer takes the whole location as the path (third branch), so new_key is 'docs/my notes.md:12::stale'. The parser reads the first token and gets path 'docs/my' with an empty line, so existing_key is 'docs/my::stale'. They never match, and a second identical entry is appended every time. `log 'Repo:src/a.go:12 — x'` has the same problem: new_key is 'Repo:src/a.go:12::x' but the parsed key is 'Repo:src/a.go:12:x'. The same truncated path also breaks annotate-pr/annotate-commit matching.
evidence: log.sh:89-91: `elif [[ "$location" == */* || "$location" == *.* ]]; then path="$location"` (whole string, spaces and :NN included). log.sh:108-114 builds new_key from that path. parse-entries.sh:136 `first_token="${location_part%%[[:space:]]*}"` and :168-171 split on the last colon.
suggested_fix: Build the candidate entry line first, run fi_parse_entry on it, and derive new_key from the parsed path and line, so writer and scanner share one key function. Alternatively reject locations containing whitespace the same way bad line specs are rejected.
needs_runtime_repro: In a scratch git repo run `found-issues log 'docs/my notes.md:12 — stale'` twice, then `found-issues list`. Expect 2 identical entries; the second run should have said 'Skipped'.

summary: The dedup key cuts the symptom at the first '(' and keeps only 50 characters. Distinct findings that mention function calls (foo()) collapse into one key, and the second finding is dropped with a misleading 'Skipped — already logged'.
failure_scenario: `log src/a.py:10 — parse() returns None on empty input`, then `log src/a.py:10 — parse() raises on unicode`. Both reduce to bare 'parse', so the key is 'src/a.py:10:parse' for both. The second, different defect is skipped and never recorded. A symptom that starts with '(' (e.g. '(optional) flag ignored') reduces to an empty string, so every such symptom at one path:line collides. The same truncation hits `list --json`: its `symptom` field for 'foo() returns null' is 'foo' (parse-entries.sh:181), and only `raw` keeps the full text.
evidence: canonicalize.sh:70 `local bare="${input%%(*}"`; parse-entries.sh:181 `symptom="${rest%%(*}"`; log.sh:169-173: `if [[ "$matched_status" == "open" ]]; then printf 'Skipped — already logged: %s\n' ...; return 0`.
suggested_fix: Strip only recognised trailing annotation groups (the fi_annotation_tail set) instead of cutting at the first '('. Use a longer or whole-symptom key. Make the Skipped message say the match was by key and show both symptoms.
needs_runtime_repro: `found-issues log 'src/a.py:10 — parse() returns None'` then `found-issues log 'src/a.py:10 — parse() raises on unicode'`. The second should print 'Skipped — already logged' and add no entry. Then `found-issues list --json | jq '.[0].symptom'` should print "parse".

summary: log writes the symptom verbatim. A symptom ending in an annotation-shaped token such as (commit: <sha>) or (PR: org/repo#N) is parsed as a flip-driving annotation, and sync then closes the entry although nothing was fixed.
failure_scenario: An agent logs: `log src/a.py:5 — regression introduced by earlier change (commit: 1a2b3c4)`. The token is the last annotation group, so fi_annotation_tail returns it as `commits`. On the next sync, 1a2b3c4 is an ancestor of the default branch, so the entry is flipped to [fixed] with a 'commit' closure immediately. The same applies to a trailing (PR: org/repo#12) once that PR is merged. Closures are irreversible. The mid-line mitigation in parse-entries.sh:192-197 does not cover a token at the end of the symptom.
evidence: log.sh:38 `local input="$*"` and :200 `local entry="- [open]${crit_flag} $(fi_today)${location_str} — $symptom"` (no sanitising). parse-entries.sh:199 `ann_tail="$(fi_annotation_tail "$line")"` feeds `commits`/`prs`. sync.sh:184-195 closes on `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.
suggested_fix: In cmd_log, reject or neutralise a symptom whose trailing groups match the recognised annotation keys other than suggested (for example replace the colon, or exit 2 with an explanation).
needs_runtime_repro: In a git repo whose HEAD is on the default branch: `found-issues log 'a.py:5 — bad (commit: '$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)')'`, then `found-issues sync --dry-run`. Expect 'Closed: 1 (… 1 commit …)'.

summary: cmd_uninstall ignores all arguments, so `found-issues uninstall --help`, `-h` or `--dry-run` performs the full destructive cleanup. This is the same class as the sync --help incident (#151) and is not in the known-flag list.
failure_scenario: An agent or operator reaches for `found-issues uninstall --help` or `--dry-run` to preview. The statusline segment is stripped from ~/.claude/statusline.sh, ~/.claude/found-issues and ~/.cache/found-issues are rm -rf'd, and the /fi alias is removed. The output is the cleanup report, not help.
evidence: uninstall.sh:26 `cmd_uninstall() {` followed immediately by `local removed_count=0`, with no `$@` handling. bin/found-issues:370 `uninstall) cmd_uninstall "$@" ;;`. Destructive calls at uninstall.sh:31, 54, 61, 70.
suggested_fix: Parse arguments in cmd_uninstall. Accept -h/--help, and optionally --dry-run. Reject unknown options with exit 2 before touching anything.
needs_runtime_repro: With HOME=$(mktemp -d), `mkdir -p $HOME/.claude/found-issues $HOME/.cache/found-issues; found-issues uninstall --help; ls -a $HOME/.claude $HOME/.cache`. Both dirs should be gone.

summary: defer swallows unknown options and the `--flag=value` forms. `--mute-until=2026-12-01` or a typo like `--mute-untl` is dropped, the entry is deferred without the mute, and the command exits 0 with a success message. promote-deferred and resolve have the same catch-all.
failure_scenario: `found-issues defer src/a.py:5 --mute-until=2026-12-01 --reason=blocked`. The `*) shift` arm discards both tokens. The entry is deferred with no mute and no reason, the output says 'Deferred 1 entry.', and a later touch triggers nudges or auto-promotes a critical entry, the exact thing the mute was meant to prevent. `defer foo --reason` with the value missing also silently proceeds (`shift 2 || break`). resolve.sh:55-58 does the same for `resolve foo --verifed human`, closing with the default `(verified: ai)`.
evidence: defer.sh:35-49: `--reason) reason="${2:-}"; shift 2 || break ;; --mute-until) ...; *) shift ;;`. resolve.sh:55-58 `*) [[ -z "$match" ]] && match="$1"; shift ;;`. promote-deferred.sh:38-43.
suggested_fix: Add `--reason=*` and `--mute-until=*` arms. Make `*)` exit 2 with 'unknown option' for any token starting with '-'. Require a value for flags that take one.
needs_runtime_repro: `found-issues defer <match> --mute-until=2026-12-01` on a ledger with one open entry, then `grep mute-until docs/found-issues.md`. Expect no match and exit 0.

summary: The documented defer example puts parentheses inside --reason. The reason annotation's `[^)]+` regexes then truncate it, and a re-defer leaves a stray ')' in the entry.
failure_scenario: commands/defer.md:54 recommends `--reason "blocked on legal review (JIRA-1234)"`, which writes `(reason: blocked on legal review (JIRA-1234))`. fi_extract_reason returns 'blocked on legal review (JIRA-1234' (cut at the first ')'). On re-defer the strip regex removes only ` (reason: blocked on legal review (JIRA-1234)`, leaving `)` glued to the line, so the entry becomes `... ) (reason: new)`. fi_annotation_tail also fails to treat the nested-paren group as an annotation, so it stops there.
evidence: defer.sh:156 `sed -E 's/ \(reason: [^)]+\)//g'`; defer.sh:160 `new_line="${new_line} (reason: ${reason})"`; parse-entries.sh:503 `re_reason='\(reason: ([^)]+)\)'`; commands/defer.md:54.
suggested_fix: Reject or replace ')' (and newlines) in --reason when writing it, for example substitute ']'. Fix the docs example to avoid parentheses.
needs_runtime_repro: `found-issues defer foo --reason 'blocked (JIRA-1)'` on an entry that already has (touched: 2026-10-01). promote-deferred it, then defer it again with `--reason x`, and inspect the line for a stray ')'.

summary: promote and promote --apply compare ledger lines verbatim. An entry that main has since flipped to [fixed], annotated or archived is reported as 'not on main', and --apply copies it back as a fresh [open] duplicate, resurrecting a closed entry.
failure_scenario: A long-lived branch was cut while entry X was [open] on main. Main later closes X as `- [fixed] ... (PR: o/r#5) (fixed: D)` or archives it. On a fresh branch cut from main, `promote --apply --from old-branch` greps the exact [open] line against the target, finds no match, and appends `- [open] X` again. The ledger now holds a [fixed] and an [open] copy, and the statusline counts it open. `promote` also lists X as needing promotion, and 'idempotent' only holds until the target copy is annotated or flipped. pre-branch-delete.sh already fixed this by comparing dedup keys, because verbatim matching false-blocked merged branches (see its header comment).
evidence: promote.sh:69 `grep -Fxq -- "$line" "$tmp" && continue`; promote.sh:157 `printf '%s' "$main_content" | grep -Fxq -- "$line"`. pre-branch-delete.sh:11-13: 'Matching: dedup key, not full-line equality ... v1.0.5 and earlier used grep -Fxq full-line matching and false-positive-blocked deletion'.
suggested_fix: Reuse the dedup-key set across main and its archive (as pre-branch-delete does) for both the listing and the --apply skip test.
needs_runtime_repro: main has `- [open] D a.py:1 — x`. Branch B is cut. On main, change the line to `- [fixed] D a.py:1 — x (verified: ai) (fixed: D)`. Cut branch C from main and run `found-issues promote --apply --from B`. Expect 'Applied 1 entry' and a duplicate [open] x.

summary: `printf '%s' "$big" | grep -Fxq` under `set -o pipefail` flakes on large ledgers. When grep -q matches early and exits, printf dies with SIGPIPE (141), the pipeline fails, and `!` turns a hit into 'not found'.
failure_scenario: With a ledger larger than the pipe buffer (16-64 KB; this repo's ledger is several hundred KB), `found-issues promote` reports early-in-file [open] entries that are verbatim on main as 'not yet on main'. The same pattern at hooks/pre-branch-delete.sh:322 (`! printf '%s' "$main_keyset" | ... grep -Fxq`) can hard-block `git branch -D` of a fully promoted branch once main_keyset exceeds the buffer (about 200-300 entries on macOS).
evidence: promote.sh:157 `if [[ -z "$main_content" ]] || ! printf '%s' "$main_content" | grep -Fxq -- "$line"; then`; bin/found-issues:29 `set -euo pipefail`; pre-branch-delete.sh:322 `elif ! printf '%s' "$main_keyset" | LC_ALL=C grep -Fxq -- "$b_key"; then`.
suggested_fix: Use a here-string (`grep -Fxq -- "$line" <<<"$main_content"`) or write the set to a temp file and `grep -Fxq -f`. Do not pipe a large builtin printf into `grep -q` under pipefail.
needs_runtime_repro: Generate a main ledger of about 1500 [open] entries (>100 KB). On a branch carrying the first entry verbatim, run `found-issues promote` repeatedly. Expect that entry to be listed as needing promotion despite being on main.

summary: The dedup scan in cmd_log fully parses every [open] entry (and every [deferred] entry when none match) with dozens of process creations each, to compare against a key that could be pre-filtered with a builtin string test.
failure_scenario: On a 100-entry ledger, each `log` costs thousands of process creations. Per entry: fi_parse_entry runs about 6 grep|sed|paste pipelines, a sed, and an fi_annotation_tail subshell (roughly 25 processes). The three `grep|head|cut` extractions add about 12. fi_dedup_key forks again, including a `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` per call via fi_canonicalize_path, plus two `tr` calls. That is about 40-45 per entry, which is very slow in Git Bash, and `log` is the hottest agent command.
evidence: log.sh:127 `e_data="$(fi_parse_entry "$entry")"`; :128-130 three `printf|grep|head|cut` pipelines; :132 `fi_dedup_key`; canonicalize.sh:37 `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel ...)"`; parse-entries.sh:203-247 the six annotation pipelines.
suggested_fix: Prefilter in bash with `[[ "$entry" == *"$path"* ]]` (or the case-folded symptom prefix) before calling fi_parse_entry. Hoist repo_root once. Replace the three grep|head|cut extractions with a single read loop over the parsed key=value lines.
needs_runtime_repro: Ledger with 100 [open] entries; run `strace -f -c -e trace=execve found-issues log x/y.py:1 — new` (or count `ps` forks via `bash -x`). Expect several thousand execve calls.

summary: fi_detect_mode runs `gh auth status`, which is a network call, before it checks its own 1-hour cache. fi_resolve_issues_file calls it on every log, defer, resolve and promote-deferred only to compare against 'local', which depends solely on whether this is a git repo.
failure_scenario: Every `log` or `defer` in a GitHub repo pays git rev-parse, git remote get-url, `gh auth status` (an HTTPS round trip), stat and date, even when the mode file is fresh. On cache expiry (hourly) it also runs `gh pr list --search`. Offline, `gh auth status` fails and the call adds latency and flips the mode to 'git'.
evidence: detect-mode.sh:86-93 `command -v gh ...; if ! gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf 'git'; return 0`, with the cache check only at :106-115. bin/found-issues:221-224 uses the result solely as `if [[ "$mode" == "local" ]]`.
suggested_fix: In fi_resolve_issues_file, test only for `git rev-parse --git-dir` and the FOUND_ISSUES_MODE=local override, and do not call fi_detect_mode. Inside fi_detect_mode, read a fresh cache before probing gh auth.
needs_runtime_repro: In a GitHub-remote repo with a fresh mode cache: `strace -f -e trace=execve found-issues defer zzz 2>&1 | grep -c 'gh'`. Expect at least one gh exec per call.

summary: The defer and promote-deferred match loops spawn 4 processes per entry, a subshell plus `tr` for the entry and the same for the loop-invariant match string. resolve.sh already hoists the match string out of the loop.
failure_scenario: `defer <match>` on 150 open entries costs 600 process creations, and the no-match path repeats the loop over deferred entries. Case-insensitive substring filtering could be one awk or tr over the whole fi_entries output.
evidence: defer.sh:84-86 `lower_entry="$(printf '%s' "$entry" | tr ...)"; lower_match="$(printf '%s' "$match" | tr ...)"` inside `while IFS= read -r entry`; promote-deferred.sh:60-62 identical. Contrast resolve.sh:81 which computes lower_match once.
suggested_fix: Compute lower_match once. Lowercase the whole fi_entries output with a single `tr`/awk call, then use bash `case`/`[[ == *x* ]]` per line.

summary: fi_resolve_default_branch ends with an unverified guess of 'main'. In a local-only repo whose default branch is master (or trunk) with no origin/HEAD and no gh, sync never closes commit-annotated entries and promote treats the real default branch as a feature branch.
failure_scenario: `git init` in a repo with no `init.defaultBranch` gives master, with no remote. After the fix is committed on master and `annotate-commit <sha>` runs, sync evaluates `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main`. That ref does not exist, the test fails silently, and the entry stays [open] forever; no warning is printed. `promote` on master compares master != 'main', lists every open entry as unpromoted, and suggests a PR 'from master to main'.
evidence: bin/found-issues:321-323 `# Last resort\n printf 'main'\n return 0`; sync.sh:190-191 `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$sha" "$default_branch" 2>/dev/null || ... "origin/$default_branch"`; promote.sh:113 `[[ "$current_branch" == "$default_branch" ]]`.
suggested_fix: In the last-resort branch, verify candidates with `git rev-parse --verify` in order: main, master, trunk, then the current branch. Otherwise return failure so callers can say 'default branch unknown' instead of silently skipping.
needs_runtime_repro: git -c init.defaultBranch=master init; log an entry for a.py:1; commit a.py; `found-issues annotate-commit HEAD --force`; `found-issues sync`. Expect 'Nothing to close' and the entry still [open].

summary: fi_handle_deferred_touch decides criticality by finding the substring '[!]' anywhere in the line. It also finds the updated entry by prefix match on the first deferred line. Either can act on the wrong entry, and a wrongly detected critical entry is auto-promoted.
failure_scenario: (a) A non-critical deferred entry whose symptom text contains '[!]' (for example 'format-enforcer rejects the [!] token') is treated as critical. When its touch count reaches the threshold it is silently auto-promoted to [open] instead of just nudging. (b) Two deferred entries from the same day where one line is a textual prefix of the other (for example symptoms 'foo' and 'foo bar' with no annotations): touching the shorter one finds the first line that starts with its text. If the longer entry comes first in the file, the count, threshold and possible auto-promote apply to the longer entry.
evidence: help.sh:174 `if [[ "$updated_entry" == *"[!]"* ]]; then is_critical=1`; help.sh:128-135 `prefix="${matched_entry%% (touched:*}" ... if [[ "$line" == "$prefix"* ]]; then updated_entry="$line"`.
suggested_fix: Test `[[ "$updated_entry" == "- [deferred] [!] "* ]]`. Locate the updated entry by line number (fi_entries ... numbered) or by the entry text with the touched annotation appended, not by a bare prefix.
needs_runtime_repro: Defer an entry whose symptom contains '[!]' with FOUND_ISSUES_DEFER_TOUCH_THRESHOLD=1, then re-log the same location and symptom. Expect 'auto-promoted to [open]' for a non-critical entry.

summary: `log --critical` on a dedup hit prints 'Skipped — already logged' and discards the critical flag, so an agent cannot escalate an existing entry. The flag only affects brand-new entries.
failure_scenario: An entry is logged as non-critical. The agent later finds it leaks a token and runs `log --critical <same location> — <same symptom>`. The CLI reports 'Skipped — already logged', the entry stays non-critical, and the statusline never shows a critical count. The same applies when the match is a [deferred] entry: the touch is recorded but no escalation happens.
evidence: log.sh:184 `[[ "$critical" == "yes" ]] && crit_flag=" [!]"` is the only use of `critical`. The open-match branch at :169-173 returns before it, and the deferred branch at :175-178 never reads it.
suggested_fix: On an [open] match with --critical, rewrite the entry to add `[!]` and report 'Escalated'. At minimum print a warning that --critical was ignored.
needs_runtime_repro: `found-issues log a.py:1 — x` then `found-issues log --critical a.py:1 — x`; `grep '\[!\]' docs/found-issues.md` returns nothing.

summary: cmd_log accepts newlines in the location or symptom. The write produces a multi-line entry whose continuation lines are not entries, and a continuation line that starts with '- [open]' injects a second entry.
failure_scenario: An agent passes a multi-line symptom (a quoted heredoc or a stack trace). The first line becomes the entry. The remaining lines are orphan text in the ledger and are ignored by the parser. Dedup and the displayed 'Logged:' line cover only part of what was written. If a continuation line starts with '- [open] ...', it becomes a separate entry that was never validated.
evidence: log.sh:38 `local input="$*"` and :42-48 split on ' — ' with no control-character check; :200 and :212 write `$symptom` as-is with `printf '%s\n'`.
suggested_fix: Collapse whitespace runs that contain newlines or tabs to a single space, or exit 2 when the input contains a newline.
needs_runtime_repro: `found-issues log a.py:1 — "line one\n- [open] 2026-01-01 b.py:2 — injected"` using $'...' quoting, then `found-issues list`. Expect an extra 'injected' entry.

summary: doctor's hook opt-out scan checks only 5 variables. It prints 'All hooks default-active' while FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ANNOTATE, FOUND_ISSUES_POST_PR_STATE, FOUND_ISSUES_HOOK_GATES, FOUND_ISSUES_AUTOSYNC_CMD and FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_MIGRATE are changing or disabling hooks.
failure_scenario: An environment sets FOUND_ISSUES_POST_PR_STATE=off, so the background sync after `gh pr merge` never runs and the counter stays stale. `found-issues doctor` still prints '✓ All hooks default-active.' and 'Recommended next' gives no hint. FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ANNOTATE=off silently reverts the hooks to prompt-only mode, with the same result.
evidence: doctor.sh:264 `for v in FOUND_ISSUES_STOP_REMINDER FOUND_ISSUES_PROMOTE_GUARD FOUND_ISSUES_FORMAT_ENFORCER FOUND_ISSUES_PRE_COMMIT FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ARCHIVE; do`. Variables read by hooks but not listed: post-bash-dispatch.sh:245/280 FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ANNOTATE, :324 FOUND_ISSUES_POST_PR_STATE; hook-gate.sh:38 FOUND_ISSUES_HOOK_GATES; session-start.sh:243 FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_MIGRATE.
suggested_fix: Generate the list from one shared array used by hooks and doctor, or add the missing variables. Treat any value other than the default, not just 'off', as worth reporting.
needs_runtime_repro: `FOUND_ISSUES_POST_PR_STATE=off FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ANNOTATE=off found-issues doctor | grep -A2 'Hook opt-outs'`. Expect 'All hooks default-active'.

summary: install-codex-hooks never checks that the hook scripts it writes exist, and it reports success. doctor has no Codex section. Stale or never-installed Codex hooks (after `codex plugin update`, or when the CLI is run from a copied location) are invisible.
failure_scenario: The hook directory is derived as FI_BIN_DIR/../hooks. If the CLI is a copy rather than a symlink (session-start.sh:200-203 supports ~/.local/bin and ~/.found-issues/cli), that is a nonexistent path. The installer writes commands pointing at missing scripts and prints 'wrote ... SessionStart -> .../session-start.sh'. After a plugin update the old versioned cache path disappears; nothing detects it, so every Codex session has dead hooks. `found-issues doctor`, the tool meant to catch this, has no Codex check, and the install output says nothing about Codex's hook-trust review (harness.sh:27-29 calls it a 'wall'), so hooks may be inert until the user approves them.
evidence: codex-hooks.sh:83-85 `printf '%s/hooks' "$(cd "$FI_BIN_DIR/.." && pwd)"`; :226-244 prints success with no `[[ -x ]]` check. doctor.sh (whole file) never reads $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json. harness.sh:27-29 'blocked by the hook-trust wall'.
suggested_fix: In install, verify each target script is a file and executable and exit non-zero otherwise. Add a doctor section that reads $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json and flags sentinel entries whose script path is missing. Print one line about Codex hook trust after install.
needs_runtime_repro: Install with `--codex-home $(mktemp -d)`, `mv` the hooks dir away, run `found-issues doctor`. Expect no mention of Codex hooks. Also run install from a copied binary and check the printed paths.

summary: The generated Codex SKILL.md writes the description as an unquoted YAML plain scalar. Several descriptions contain ': ' (and one has ' #N'), which is invalid YAML for strict loaders, so the skills may fail to load or be truncated in Codex.
failure_scenario: codex-skills/fi-sync/SKILL.md line 3 is `description: Reconcile the ledger with reality: flip [open] entries ...`. The ': ' inside a block-mapping value is a YAML error ('mapping values are not allowed here'). fi-log ('observations: to change'), fi-fix ('as a batch: re-verify'), fi-annotate-commit ('HEAD: run it') and fi-annotate-pr (both ': ' and the comment-starting " #N" in 'PR #N') are affected too. If Codex parses frontmatter with serde_yaml, those five core skills are skipped, or description is cut at ' #'. Claude Code is lenient about frontmatter. Codex may not be.
evidence: gen-codex-skills.sh:71 `printf 'description: %s\n' "$desc"`. Generated lines: codex-skills/fi-sync/SKILL.md:3 'Reconcile the ledger with reality: flip ...'; fi-log:3 'Only for NEW observations: to change ...'; fi-annotate-pr:3 "like 'PR #N' in an entry".
suggested_fix: Emit the description as a double-quoted YAML string, escaping backslashes and double quotes, or as a folded block scalar. Add a test that parses every generated frontmatter with a real YAML parser.
needs_runtime_repro: `for f in codex-skills/*/SKILL.md; do python3 -c "import sys,yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('$f').read().split('---')[1])" || echo BAD $f; done`. Expect BAD for fi-sync, fi-log, fi-fix, fi-annotate-pr and fi-annotate-commit. Confirm in a real Codex session with `codex` skill listing.

summary: cmd_uninstall (the $fi-uninstall path for Codex) never removes the entries install-codex-hooks wrote into $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json. Its next-steps text covers only Claude's /plugin commands. After the plugin and CLI are removed, those hooks dangle.
failure_scenario: A Codex user runs `$fi-uninstall` and then removes the plugin. hooks.json still has 4 commands with the `env FOUND_ISSUES_HARNESS=codex` prefix pointing at a deleted cache directory. Every Codex session and Bash tool call then runs a missing script. Because the CLI is no longer on PATH, `found-issues uninstall-codex-hooks` cannot be run afterwards, so the user must hand-edit the JSON.
evidence: uninstall.sh:26-92 covers statusline, onboarding dir, mode cache and the fi alias only. The closing text at :79-91 lists only `/plugin uninstall` and `/plugin marketplace remove`. AGENTS.md documents `found-issues uninstall-codex-hooks` as a separate manual step.
suggested_fix: Have cmd_uninstall call the codex-hook removal when $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json contains the sentinel, or at least print a line telling the user to run `found-issues uninstall-codex-hooks` before removing the plugin.
needs_runtime_repro: install-codex-hooks into a temp --codex-home (or FOUND_ISSUES_CODEX_HOME), run `found-issues uninstall`, and check that hooks.json still contains the sentinel commands.

summary: `merged="$(jq ...)"` runs under errexit. When hooks.json is invalid JSON, jq's non-zero exit aborts the script immediately. The 'leaving it untouched' message and exit code 5 below are unreachable, and the user sees only a raw jq parse error. The uninstall path has the same issue.
failure_scenario: `~/.codex/hooks.json` has a trailing comma. `found-issues install-codex-hooks` prints jq's 'parse error: ...' and exits with jq's status (2). It never prints 'failed to produce valid JSON ... leaving it untouched' and never returns the documented 5. Scripts or agents that key on exit 5 misread it.
evidence: codex-hooks.sh:206 `merged="$(jq --argjson new ... "$hooks_file")"` followed by the guard at :216-219; :270 `stripped="$(jq --arg sentinel ... "$hooks_file")"` followed by the guard at :272-275. bin/found-issues:29 `set -euo pipefail`.
suggested_fix: Capture with `merged="$(jq ...)" || merged=""` (or `if ! merged=$(...)`) so the guarded error path runs.
needs_runtime_repro: `printf '{bad' > $T/hooks.json; found-issues install-codex-hooks --codex-home $T; echo $?`. Expect 2 (or 5, depending on jq) with only jq's message, not the 'leaving it untouched' text.

summary: Mode detection falls back to 'git' whenever the remote host string lacks 'github.com' or `gh auth status` fails (offline, a stale second account). In 'git' mode sync never resolves repo_id, so PR annotations silently stop closing. doctor prints 'Detected mode: git' with a pass marker and no explanation. A cache file that is empty or mid-write is returned verbatim for an hour.
failure_scenario: (1) The remote is an SSH alias (`git@github-work:org/repo.git`) or GitHub Enterprise: it is classified 'git', fi_repo_id returns 1, and every (PR: ...) entry in the ledger is never evaluated, with no warning. (2) `gh auth status` exits non-zero offline or when a secondary account's token is stale, so mode flips to 'git' and sync silently skips PR closure until auth recovers. (3) `cat "$cache_file"` of an empty file (a truncating `>` race with a parallel session) returns '' as the mode for up to an hour, so repo_id stays empty in sync.
evidence: detect-mode.sh:80 `[[ -z "$remote_url" || "$remote_url" != *"github.com"* ]] ... printf 'git'`; :90-93 `if ! gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf 'git'`; :111-113 `cat "$cache_file"` with no emptiness check. sync.sh:70-72 `if [[ "$mode" == "github-pr" || ... ]]; then repo_id=...`, and :148 requires repo_id before any PR check. doctor.sh:246-247 prints the mode with $section_pass.
suggested_fix: Have doctor warn when the ledger has (PR: ...) annotations and the mode is not a github-* mode, and state why. Treat a gh auth failure as 'unknown' rather than 'git', and validate the cache contents against the four known modes.
needs_runtime_repro: Set the origin to `git@github-alias:o/r.git`, add `(PR: o/r#1)` to an open entry, run `found-issues doctor` and `found-issues sync --dry-run`. Expect mode 'git' with a pass marker and no PR evaluation.

summary: Ledger rewrites (defer, resolve, promote-deferred, append-touch, sync) build the temp file in the system temp dir with `mktemp -t` and then `mv` it over the ledger. That is not an atomic rename when the temp dir is on another filesystem, and the new ledger inherits mode 0600. codex-hooks.sh creates its temp file in the target directory for exactly this reason.
failure_scenario: On Linux with tmpfs /tmp and the repo on ext4, `mv` falls back to copy-then-unlink. An interruption, ENOSPC, or a statusline `status` read from a parallel session mid-copy sees a truncated ledger, and entries can be lost. After any mutation the ledger also changes from 0644 to 0600.
evidence: defer.sh:146 `tmp="$(mktemp -t fi-defer.XXXXXX)"` and :172 `mv "$tmp" "$file"`; the same pattern in resolve.sh:139/153, parse-entries.sh:684/738 and resolve.sh:171/189. Contrast codex-hooks.sh:162-171 ('mktemp is created in the SAME directory as the target ... atomic').
suggested_fix: Create the temp file with `mktemp "$file.XXXXXX"` in the ledger's directory, and copy the original mode (chmod --reference or `stat`) before the rename.
needs_runtime_repro: With TMPDIR on tmpfs and the repo elsewhere, `strace -f -e trace=rename,renameat2 found-issues defer <m>` shows EXDEV on the rename. `stat -c %a docs/found-issues.md` before and after shows 644 becoming 600.

summary: Neither promote nor the branch-delete guard considers [deferred] entries. A branch-only entry that was deferred before the branch is abandoned and deleted is lost without any warning.
failure_scenario: On a feature branch the agent logs an issue and then `defer`s it, which is a legitimate parking action. The branch is never merged and is deleted. pre-branch-delete only inspects `[open]` lines, and `promote` and `promote --apply` only list or copy `[open]` entries ('a [deferred] entry carries defer-cycle state that belongs to its branch'). The deferred entry, with its touch history and reason, disappears with the branch and nothing blocks the delete.
evidence: promote.sh:60-62 `[[ "$line" =~ ^-\ \[open\] ]] || continue`; pre-branch-delete.sh:313 `if [[ "$line" =~ ^-[[:space:]]+\[open\] ]]; then`; commands/promote.md:59-60 '[fixed] and [deferred] entries are deliberately left behind'.
suggested_fix: Include [deferred] entries in the guard and in --apply, preserving their annotations, with the dedup-key check so merged ones are not re-copied.
needs_runtime_repro: On a branch: `found-issues log a.py:1 — x`, `found-issues defer a.py:1`, commit, then (with the branch not merged) `git branch -D <branch>` via the hook path. Expect the hook to allow the delete.
